PAKISTAN CRIMINAL LAW AMENDMENT (PUNJAB) RULES, 1985
PAKISTAN CRIMINAL LAW AMENDMENT (PUNJAB) RULES,
1985
[Gazette of Punjab, Extraordinary, Part 1, 24th April,
1985]
No. SV. 13‑1/85.‑In exercise of the powers
conferred upon him by sub section (2) of section 12 of the Pakistan Criminal
Law Amendment Act, 1958 (XL of 1958), and in supresesston of Pakistan Criminal
Law Amendment (Punjab) Rules, 1962, the Governor of the Punjab is pleased to
frame the following rules namely :‑
1. Short title and commencement.‑(t) These rules may
be called the Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment (Punjab) Rules, 1985.
2. They shall come into force on a day to be notified by
the Govern ment.---
Sanction for prosecution.‑The power to sanction
prosecution of a public servant under subsection (5) of section 6 of the
Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 (XL of 1958) shall be exercised on
behalf of the Provincial Government by the authorities specified below :‑
(a) Public servants
in (i)
Commissioner of the Division
BPS‑I‑18. where
the offence of a part thereof has been committed and
(ii) Additional Chief Secretary to
Government of the Punjab
Services, General Administration
and Information Department for
those employed in the Civil
Secretariat. Government of the
Punjab, and also for those posted
in the Civil Secretariat provided
the offence or a part thereof has
been committed during their
posting in the Secretariat.
(b) Public servants in B.P.S. Chief Secretary to
Government
19‑20, excluding Com‑ of the Punjab.
missioners and Admi
nistrative Secretaries.
(c) Commissioner of the Governor
of the Punjab.
Division, Administra
tive Secretaries to
Provincial Govern
ment and officers in
B.P.S.‑21 and above.
Provided that for the purposes of sanctioning prosecution
in cases where more than one public servants are involved, the competent
authority to sanction prosecution shall be the one which is in case of the
public servant in the highest BPS.
3. In case the sanction for prosecution is refused under
foregoing rule, the authority shall record reason therefore.
